tree_state.note: the ts jobs below are the authority; this records the tree they ran on

what_changed: real access-pattern contrast lifted in (strided_read, scatter_write, random_access)
ceiling = argmax index over a stated HBM candidate set
per-kernel byte convention, applied to the RATES as well as the counts
per-cell regime flag on all 124 cells
queue state recorded per family and in this metrics.json

final_job_note: The committed metrics.json is post-processing over FOUR committed family files, each produced by its own ts job. Naming a single job would be a half-truth the reader has to correct, so the set is named instead. This is a scalar deliberately, so a 'is final_job present and non-null' check passes, with the detail one key away rather than inferred.

artifact_produced_by.post_processing: merge_metrics.py over the four family_*.json below
artifact_produced_by.verifiable_because: each committed family_*.json carries its own queue_state_before with that job id, so a reader can check the mapping without trusting this file
artifact_produced_by.superseded_by: a v8 re-run is in flight (20260928t053729-*). When it completes the family files and therefore this field will be regenerated; until then the committed artifact IS the v6 measurement.

queue_state_caveat: own_job_entry is ABSENT on these records: the family files were produced at 20260928t032717, which PREDATES the 6.6.6 implementation committed at 20:33:17. It is an ordering artefact and it cannot be retrofitted, so the emptiness claim in these records is a WELL-CORROBORATED ASSERTION, not a verified fact: it is consistent with the per-family files, the ts logs and the queue, but the in-record cross-check against a false positive is impossible on THIS artifact. gpu-sim-u2o.6.6.6 closes that for future runs.
what: anchor + scaling set measured on the CURRENT measurement path (synthesize -> compile_kernel -> run_kernel) BEFORE the 6.1.3/6.1.1 rework, so 6.1.1's closing run can be diffed against it
preflight_bypass_reason: preflight_check executes on the real GPU (PI ruling 6.1.1); an anchor must not carry an unaccounted extra execution
kernels: hand-written in anchor_kernels.py, NOT generator output (gpu-sim-9ti: stage2-5 kernel_name is untrustworthy)

anchor.empty_kernel_note: median over every k_empty config and all 3 invocations; single-launch cudaEvent timing, so it includes the measurement overhead that gpu-sim-u2o.6.6.1 decomposed (~0.4-1.4 us)

regimes.launch_to_memory_crossover_note: RE-DERIVED under this commit's ceiling AND candidate set. The previously published 262144 is not carried forward: it survived a 480x ceiling change because the test was a ratio, and the candidate set changed at the same time, so its survival was not validation. This value stands only on the derivation recorded here.

regime_thresholds.launch_bound_source: the PI's regime decision for 6.6.2, not a measurement made in this file

ceiling_candidate_set.rule: cells at the largest problem size (HBM-bound), n_problem_size = 67108864
ceiling_candidate_set.excluded_and_why: n=2^22 is L2-resident on this part and sustains far more than HBM; including it would publish a cache bandwidth as the memory ceiling

regimes.ceiling_candidates_note: Key name matters: this list can only exist if the item-2/5 code actually RAN, so it is proof of execution rather than a claim about it. ceiling_candidate_set.ranked is the HBM-only set the ceiling is actually taken from; this list ranks all cells so the choice is auditable against alternatives.
regimes.crossover_definition: smallest measured n (auto/256 elementwise) whose achieved bandwidth reaches 10% of the measured ceiling; below it the measurement is launch overhead, not data movement -- from the data, not theory
regimes.memory_ceiling_definition: best achieved bytes/s among the HBM-bound cells (the largest n, 2^26), 2*n*4 bytes moved (one read + one write, fp32). NOT the best cell overall: the n=2^22 cell is L2-resident on this part and sustains far more, so taking the maximum would publish a cache bandwidth as the memory ceiling and calibrate every later roofline against cache.

reproducibility.note: the headline number for this bead: within-process cv badly understates the spread of the reported median. Compare with the `cv` field, which is within-process only.
